attributes.name: [GCP Cloud Run OTel] Request latency under 1 second 99% rolling 30 days
attributes.description: Tracks the share of successful (2xx and 3xx) requests to each Google Cloud Run service that complete in under 1000 ms inside the container, from the run.googleapis.com/request_latencies histogram (milliseconds). Good events are histogram observations from 0 to 1000 ms; total events are all observations. 5xx responses are excluded because the availability SLO covers them. 1xx (WebSocket upgrade) and 4xx responses are also excluded. The objective is 99% of requests over a rolling 30-day window, per service in each GCP project and region. Limitations: request_latencies starts when a request reaches a running instance, so it excludes cold-start time (see container/startup_latencies) and time spent pending in the load balancer during scale-out. Services with long-lived streaming responses (server-sent events, gRPC streaming, HTTP/2 streams) record the whole stream duration, so exclude them or raise the threshold. GCP buckets this distribution with a growth factor of 1.1, so the 1000 ms boundary is accurate to about 5%. Tune the threshold to each service's latency budget.

params.filter: data_stream.dataset: "gcp.cloudrun.otel" and resource.attributes.service_name: * and attributes.response_code_class: ("2xx" or "3xx")
